title: Night One
subtitle: A crew becomes responsible for something small.
summary: Commission Aurora, plant Alo and Tara, prepare for a 36-hour scenario night and survive a labelled historical storm replay. First bloom closes the night and opens the mystery of N.
emotionalArc: Curiosity -> shared care -> prepared fear -> controlled crisis -> earned relief.
openingHook: The battery is full, sunlight is spilling, and the first decision changes the room before anyone gives a speech.
transitionOut: Earth contact returns days later on April 30. Tara opens and the recorded request becomes a pollination problem.

scenes.title: Sunlight We Cannot Keep
scenes.prose:
The first thing Aurora asks of Mei is not her name. It is where the spare sunlight should go. A gold band has reached the top of the battery display, while the mast outside is still producing. Kai reaches for a switch, then stops when Amara points to the overflow arrow. A full store cannot promise to hold more.

The player traces the diagram to the air tank or planting bay. Both are safe commissioning choices. The air gauge rises if they store oxygen; the empty garden glows if they light the bay. A comparison preview also shows what spilling the spare supply means. The result remains visible while the crew accepts its assignment.

Ferreira watches from an Earth console. She asks each specialist to describe one responsibility and one limit. Mei notices four mugs with no names. Aurora feels borrowed, but its first decision already belongs to them. Before anyone celebrates, Rafi turns the emergency card towards every seat. Their first shared achievement is knowing how to stop.

scenes.title: The Rule That Works Without Earth
scenes.location: Mission table and Safe Room doorway
scenes.prose:
Rafi places four name tokens on the Safe Room board. None is an oxygen token, and none can be traded for a better score. They stand for people. A harmless fault appears on a disconnected practice panel. The player must find which information comes from a local sensor, which is stored guidance, and which requires Earth.

Kai points to Ferreira's screen. What happens when that rectangle disappears? Rafi shows him the printed retreat sequence. Emergency rules, suit radios and the station network remain local. Losing the direct Earth path removes conversation, not the crew's ability to care for itself. Amara tests the labelled acknowledgement without activating a hazard. Mei checks that the gardening bench can be made safe before anyone leaves it.

The team rehearses a quiet roll call. Nobody sprints. The player explains the stored card in their own order and discovers the same instruction beneath both views: experiments wait when the habitat cannot support them. Ferreira asks for a local stop decision before approving the assignment. Responsibility includes the right to pause.

learning.explain: Communications and life support are separate systems.
learning.transfer: A school emergency plan should not depend on one phone.

scenes.title: A Label Older Than Our Names
scenes.prose:
The inventory lamp blinks beside a drawer that seems too small to contain a story. Inside lies a sealed dry packet with two seeds, Bengali lettering and a single initial. Mei reads the word for light. Kai proposes Light One and Light Two. Amara writes two blank identity labels before anyone can make the joke permanent.

A historical card shows cotton germinating in China's sealed Chang'e-4 experiment in 2019. Mei separates that real seedling from their future flowering goal.

The player examines the seal and storage record, then copies the packet label. The original stays protected. A moisture probe offers a confident-looking number, but confidence is not a reference. Mei calibrates it against the provided reference sample before it touches a planting cassette. The reading changes; a measurement becomes useful because its basis is visible.

One cassette belongs to the exterior pressurised test chamber; the other belongs to the indoor reference bay. Neither seed will sit in lunar vacuum. The player compares the atmosphere diagrams and notices how much machinery the word outside conceals. Warmth, pressure, water and light still need supplying. The initial remains unanswered. For now, a more important question is whether the station can give two old seeds a fair beginning.

dialogue.speaker: Rafi

scenes.title: Two Places for a Beginning
scenes.location: Garden glove ports and indoor reference bay
scenes.prose:
Mei guides the first seed into its cassette through the glove ports. The movement is small enough that the player can take their time. Kai holds the work light steady instead of helping twice. Amara reads the label back, and Rafi confirms the transfer lid is latched before the next seal opens. The sequence never asks a learner to imitate an unsafe vacuum experiment.

The player plants Alo in the exterior test chamber and Tara in the indoor reference bay, one compatible plant per cassette. Their cards record the same seed lot and different environments. A notebook asks what the team will observe. The task is not to declare which plant is better, but to keep observations and conditions together. Temperature, moisture and lighting accompany each photograph.

When Mei presses both names onto their holders, two empty circles become responsibilities. Tara receives her own close view, not a spare-plant thumbnail. The player checks both service connections and sees that both depend on the same careful crew. The packet returns to protected storage. Its unanswered initial can wait; the next care visit cannot.

dialogue.line: Alo outside. Tara inside. A star beside our light.

dialogue.speaker: Amara

dialogue.speaker: Kai

dialogue.speaker: Rafi

scenes.title: An Important Scientific Lamp
scenes.prose:
Kai checks the corridor switch once, then again. Mei notices the second click but leaves space before asking. He describes the lamp as important scientific equipment. Rafi considers this, retrieves a hand light and hangs it handle-out beside the locker. He does not make Kai explain a fear in front of the whole team.

The player tests the light, marks its home on the equipment board and begins a dated care sequence. Each visit brings a task: compare a root photograph, inspect a connection, record chamber conditions or notice a new leaf. The transitions show actual care days. Buds do not appear because a button was held for fourteen seconds. Time advances only at explicit date cards, after the required work is recorded.

As the corridor becomes familiar, the crew's objects acquire places. Amara's stylus returns to its clip. Mei's pencil stays near both plant records. The spare light remains where Kai can find it without asking. Beside the latest photograph the player places the first. The difference is earned by the intervening record: care has a rhythm before it has a crisis.

scenes.title: The Night Has a Shape
scenes.prose:
Amara unfolds the training schedule across the table. Two daylight work shifts stand before five dark shifts. The display calls the coming thirty-six-hour interval a scenario based on polar science. It does not claim the crew has already computed Aurora's exact sky. A source tab separates the published illumination map from the authored schedule.

The player arranges Sun, Earth-link and station-system cards on separate tracks. A dark array does not mean Earth has already disappeared. An Earth outage does not switch off the local air maker. Once the cards align, Kai can describe the night without treating it as one enormous blackout. There will be named stages, stored reserves and people on each watch.

Mei adds the garden's needs. Rafi adds shelter access and the familiar hand light. Amara asks everyone to explain one dependency from another role. This reveals a mistake while it is still a drawing: protecting the shelter for too long can leave irrigation unavailable. The player corrects the schedule before any resource changes are committed. The low Sun is still present. Preparation has time to be an action.

scenes.title: Air Before the Jar Spills
scenes.location: Air console and mast status panel
scenes.prose:
The battery fills quickly in daylight, exactly as it did during commissioning. Amara asks Kai to watch the overflow arrow instead of admiring the full gauge. Her role card explains that useful air can be made now. Kai's card explains the dark interval the stored energy must support. Neither card solves the whole schedule alone.

The player compares two plans in the same preview. Both begin from the fixed April 25 survival state, not the earlier commissioning exercise. Production, storage cap and spending appear in their proper order. An animation follows energy into the air maker and then points to the oxygen store. Mei watches the lamp setting; a convenient air plan still affects the garden.

Each cadet gives a recommendation. In Solo, every role card is available; in Class, groups share private printed cards. No solution depends on another controller. The player commits daylight shift 1 and stages the shift 2 plan without advancing it. The shelter drill is still ahead of that second commitment. The night remains ahead, its reserves visible. Amara does not call the result perfect. She calls it a plan the team can explain and therefore revise. Kai writes the reason beside the setting, giving the next watch something more useful than a number.

dialogue.line: We can keep air we make now. We cannot keep overflow.

dialogue.line: Same full jar. Better destination.

dialogue.speaker: Mei

learning.explain: Compare whole plans rather than separate best cases.
learning.transfer: Agree on a single shared budget before promising separate outcomes.

scenes.title: Borrowing Includes Returning
scenes.prose:
Rafi begins the drill by pointing to the doorway and asking everyone to count themselves in. The feed identifies the historical 2017 source of the storm warning. It is not a newly measured flare in 2046. With that distinction visible, the team practises the responses the scenario will test.

The player follows water from the garden reservoir into the shelter wall and back in a reversible demonstration. Another preview shows supplies positioned as shielding. Practice spends no survival resources and leaves no free permanent crate wall. Amara reads the post-drill state aloud, proving the exercise has not silently improved the actual baseline.

Mei asks why a wall that protects people can hurt a plant. Rafi points to the shared reservoir. The same water cannot occupy both places. Their problem is conservation and timing, not deciding whose life matters. Crew sheltering is mandatory. Inside that boundary, the player rehearses the controls and marks a return-water reminder. Kai draws its arrow like a returning road. The joke makes the obligation memorable. Each cadet demonstrates the same rule through a different view. Only after the drill does the player commit the staged second daylight shift; the date card reaches 18:00 and the masts approach sunset.

learning.transfer: Plan the return of shared equipment before borrowing it.

scenes.title: The Horizon Closes One Door
scenes.prose:
The mast stops producing, and the station grows quieter without becoming dead. Fans continue. The hand light remains in its marked place. Kai lets the player inspect reserves before switching off a decorative lamp. He asks when light will return. Amara points to their schedule instead of promising he will stop being afraid.

Mei's role card arrives in the first dark shift. In this scenario, cold and thirst are Alo's immediate threats; borrowed shielding water affects irrigation. Rafi's warning and Kai's budget must now be read alongside it. The player compares two complete plans, including the later cost of returning water. Heat settings remain genuine options under the locked rules. The story does not manufacture one moral answer.

Earth contact ends at its separate shift gate. The crew reads back Ferreira's last available instruction before the channel greys out. Stored guidance is labelled beside the unavailable live-link button. No new Earth voice slips through. Kai reaches towards the familiar lamp, then opens the plan instead. The next shift is committed with the local crew present. This loss of contact matters, but it is a loss they prepared to understand.

scenes.title: The Choice Inside the Rules
scenes.storyTime: Dark shift 5; historical 2017 event replay UTC
scenes.prose:
The alarm is a change in an instrument, not a wall of glowing projectiles outside. Its historical-replay label remains beside the trace. Rafi's voice loses its apologetic lift. He calls four names and waits for four answers before any exposed phase can be committed.

The response panel offers the canonical prepared WAIT, PUMP or STACK actions as allowed by the actual state. The player inspects the forecast, selects one response and confirms it. Clicking quickly cannot collect the full benefits of several exclusive actions. Assisted modes remove the action timer while preserving reasoning and outcomes. No reward requires tolerating a panic effect.

Kai reaches for a second switch. Mei asks him to read their chosen action back. That interruption turns frantic movement into a team decision. Inside the Safe Room, the player follows shared resources and the meter, hearing suit and cabin sounds rather than exterior wind. The exposure score is a game abstraction, not a medical radiation dose. The response resolves under the same rules used in rehearsal. The crew has not defeated the Sun. It has made a controlled decision inside a prepared safety system.

learning.transfer: Follow an agreed drill sequence rather than inventing simultaneous tasks.

scenes.title: Send the Water Home
scenes.location: Garden service line and mission table
scenes.prose:
The alarm eases, but the wall does not empty itself. Mei studies the garden line while Amara checks which exposure step has actually finished. The player must respect the rule ordering. Water cannot be drained before the exposure it was meant to shield resolves. Afterwards, keeping it forever would be another mistake.

The display shows the same reservoir and plant forecast discussed before Earth-set. The player checks the remaining plan, returns water at a valid gate and commits the final shifts. An animation follows flow back to the garden. Kai watches the battery approach a low value without narrating automatic failure. Exactly zero stored energy is distinct from an unpaid demand causing blackout. The system determines the result.

Alo lost and Mission stopped receive respectful closures and causal reviews. They never advance this expedition with an unexplained replacement flower. A local checkpoint restores the complete state for a supported retry. On the successful route, Mei records which choices kept the crew safe and which kept the bud alive. The last task before sunrise is not applause. It is confirming that opening the chamber's viewing shutter will be safe.

scenes.title: Alo Needs a Friend
scenes.location: Chamber shutter and Tara reference bay
scenes.prose:
The first strip of returning light meets a closed shutter. Mei asks the player to check chamber conditions before opening it. After all that waiting, the story gives this small safety action the same dignity as the alarm. Only then does a yellow mustard flower appear.

The player tags the bloom photograph. That event triggers a stored care message. The recorder has not predicted the future, and nobody is calling through the absent Earth link. A voice signed N. congratulates whoever is hearing it, then says Alo needs a friend. Mei looks towards the indoor bay. Tara's bud has been receiving its own care all along. Now its place becomes a new question.

The debrief separates historical storm records, scenario schedule and fictional station. It names the crew's actual decisions and earned Bloom or Golden Bloom result. Assistance receives the same ending access. Mei puts the image beside the packet without replacing its unknown initial with a guess. Outside, nothing has become easy. Inside, Aurora has become their station. A living flower and a complete first-night outcome give the player a reason to enter the next room.

title: Be the Bee
subtitle: A flower becomes a partnership, and an object becomes evidence.
summary: Tara flowers as Earth contact returns. The crew carries out three sealed reciprocal pollen runs across seven care days, records a testable inheritance prediction and reconstructs an older horticulture recording. The evening ends with a quake.
emotionalArc: Recognition -> patient precision -> curiosity -> tentative personal connection -> decisive reprioritising.
openingHook: The next important flower opens in the other room while everyone is admiring the first.
transitionOut: No date jump follows the quake. The four accounted-for cadets begin testing the changed pressure warning at 22:05.

scenes.title: The Star in the Other Room
scenes.location: Tara reference bay and Earth console
scenes.prose:
Tara opens while everyone is still choosing a place for Alo's photograph. Mei notices the second flower before the Earth console lights. When contact returns, Ferreira's praise arrives days after sunrise, exactly when a conversation is possible again. The delay gives the player time to understand that the crew's achievement did not require a live audience.

The player compares Tara's identity card with Alo's. Both are compatible individuals of the selected mustard cultivar, but one flower cannot simply make the full experiment happen alone. A sealed protocol identifies pollen donor, recipient and the parts to be observed. Mei turns the recorder's instruction into a question the team can investigate rather than an order to obey blindly.

Kai suggests placing the two chambers together. Amara points to their separate services and research purposes. Moving the whole experiment would change more than one thing and create work they have not planned. Instead, the crew will move pollen in a controlled carrier. Tara receives a new photograph beside Alo's. The page now looks less like a heroic portrait and more like a partnership, which is precisely the discovery Mei wants everyone to see.

scenes.title: A Bee Is More Than a Costume

Rafi folds a paper bee and puts it beside the protocol. Mei smiles, then asks what the real bee's useful job would be. The game accepts words and shapes together; recognising a yellow spot by colour alone is never required.

Amara lays out two clean brushes with separate labels. One will move compatible pollen from Tara to Alo; the other will support the reciprocal transfer without mixing the records. Mei describes her grandmother's hand-pollination work in an orchard where pollinators were scarce. She does not claim every bee in China disappeared. A remembered family action becomes a carefully bounded example.

The player rehearses on a nonliving model first, identifying contact points and checking that both plant records agree on direction. A wrong model placement returns an explanation rather than damaging a real flower. Kai tests a carrier latch and discovers the challenge is not making bee noises. It is delivering a small biological material without losing the atmosphere or the evidence. Rafi leaves the paper bee on the bench as a reminder of the function they are learning to replace.

Rafi puts the sketch beside the station diagram, letting the player discover what the line has omitted. Pollen is tiny. The atmosphere supporting both plants is not optional.

The player checks space-weather status, prepares the closed carrier and traces each transfer boundary before committing the first run. A mock latch indicator offers both an icon and a word. Two boundaries cannot be opened together. The interface previews one complete reciprocal cycle and its single canonical route charge, instead of charging the same cycle again at every animation cut.

Amara asks which observations will prove completion. Mei lists both plant identities, both transfer directions and the dated care record. Kai adds the carrier check without making a joke. The crew can now explain the route from memory, but the checklist remains available. Planning has earned them confidence rather than permission to skip verification. The player closes the last practice boundary and sees both chamber pressure indicators unchanged. Their first pollination visit is ready to be useful because getting there and coming back are part of the same mission.

The return leg uses the separately labelled brush for the reciprocal direction. Rafi keeps the route record and watches the pressure confirmations. Kai holds the carrier in its cradle until the label has been read back. Every small action has a purpose: identity, containment or useful contact. The player finishes the entire reciprocal cycle before the scenario records its route charge.

Afterwards, both flowers still look like flowers. There is no immediate shower of seeds to reward the final click. Mei saves a contact image and the date. Rafi asks whether it worked. Amara distinguishes what they have verified from what they must wait to observe. The transfer procedure is complete; seed development is a later biological result. The first real bee run ends with a good record and a reason to keep caring tomorrow.

scenes.title: Seven Dates, Three Visits
scenes.location: Paired care stations and transfer route

A strip of seven date spaces runs beneath the paired flower photographs. Three contain the mark for a reciprocal bee run; all seven require care observations. The player reads the difference before advancing the calendar. Daily tending is not the same task as transferring pollen, and repeating a transfer at every visit would not make the record more accurate.

On the next care day, the chamber trend asks for a reference comparison. Another day asks the player to compare leaf and flower photographs. The second and third reciprocal cycles occur on their scheduled dates, May 3 and May 6, following the same sealed protocol under fresh weather checks. The remaining visits vary the observation rather than requiring a mechanical rerun of every tool animation.

Kai tries to make a bee stamp line perfectly straight. Mei leaves one slightly crooked mark because it records a real completed visit. Amara checks dates instead of handwriting. By the final card, the player can explain what stayed controlled and what changed with time. The game compresses the calendar openly, retaining each required task and both plants' conditions. Seven days pass through care, not through a progress bar that silently spends oxygen while the reader pauses.

scenes.title: A Prediction Is Not a Promise
scenes.prose:
Alo's stem carries purple pigment; Tara's stem is green. Amara asks the player to record a prediction about the descendants, and Kai offers the confident answer first. Mei asks what their observation can actually prove. Two visible traits and a family relationship do not establish every genetic detail of the plants.

The player chooses a prediction, writes a reason using the available evidence and marks what would count as a surprise. The interface permits uncertainty. It does not force a textbook ratio onto a fictional pair whose complete genotype has not been established. Amara keeps the original prediction beside a blank future observation panel rather than replacing it with a green success tick.

Rafi wonders whether being wrong will remove a mission star. The experiment answers through its structure: a supported prediction and honest comparison are the achievement. Actual descendant colours will be recorded in Chapter 4, after seed harvest and intervening care. Nobody opens a pod early to hurry the evidence. The player saves the dated prediction and sees a thread connect it to the family-tree page. It is a promise to look again, not a promise that nature will obey the first guess.

scenes.title: Not Tomorrow's Seeds
scenes.prose:
Kai puts a clean seed tray beside the care strip and asks whether tomorrow is harvest day. Amara says no before he finishes drawing the label. Mei brings up the growth sequence: flowers, developing pods, mature pods, drying and harvest. The player matches each stage to an observation instead of moving a calendar slider until the answer appears.

One image shows a young, unflowered seedling with curled leaves from the old trial. Another shows their current pollinated flower. A third is a reference illustration of mature pods. The task is to explain which image belongs to which stage and which evidence the crew does not yet possess. The sequence gives a practical reason to continue care without turning waiting into compulsory idle play.

Rafi places the paper bee beside the finished record. Its folded wing brushes the horticulture recorder and exposes a familiar equipment number. The player notices that the recorder and an old trial card share an identifier. This is a physical link, not a guess about a person's initials. Mei saves the life-cycle entry before opening the service label. Their next investigation begins because they have learned to look closely at their ordinary tools, while the living experiment continues at its own pace.

A lifted corner on the recorder's newer service sticker reveals part of an older plate. Kai almost peels it back. Mei hands him the camera instead. They need the information without destroying the original surface, because a good mystery can survive careful handling.

The player photographs the serial plate, maintenance date and trial-stage chart, then places copies on the evidence board. Each card carries its source object and uncertainty. The older chart states that the reproductive stage was not reached. Alo's bloom therefore does not become a false achievement when an earlier plant trial is discovered. The old experiment had seedlings; their own experiment has flowers.

Amara asks the team to separate three questions: which device is this, when was it used, and what stage did the trial reach? Matching a number answers the first, not all three. The player can inspect a tempting unsupported card naming a possible owner, but it remains excluded until evidence exists. The final board leaves a clean empty space where a person might later belong. The mystery grows stronger because the team knows exactly what it knows and has not filled the rest with a confident story.

Three recorder files have fields in the wrong places: date, device identifier and voice channel. Amara asks the player to reconstruct the mapping using the physical evidence just collected. Nothing requires guessing a password or recognising a face the player has never seen.

The correct date connects the record to 2034. The correct identifier connects it to the horticulture recorder. The channel assignment separates an engineering instruction from a gardener's personal note. A checksum confirmation tests that the restored copy is internally intact; it does not certify every historical interpretation. The original remains untouched while the player works on a local copy.

Kai proposes naming the file after the person he thinks he hears. Mei chooses the equipment label instead. The anonymous voices will be heard once the mapping is supported, not once the team invents the most dramatic explanation. Rafi reads the reconstruction steps aloud so a second crew member could repeat them. When the playback button becomes available, the player has earned access by making evidence usable. The reward is not a solved identity. It is a reliable fragment with a date, a source and a clear limit on what it can tell them.

scenes.title: A Voice With Younger Edges
scenes.prose:
The restored engineering voice orders a safe retreat from an earlier trial. It sounds younger than Ferreira, but its clipped care with instructions is familiar. Kai turns towards the Earth screen. The player can replay the passage or read its transcript, and the date remains visible above both.

Another channel contains the gardener's memory of yellow mustard fields in Bangladesh. The signature is N. The recording speaks of bringing some of that light to the Moon. Mei looks at the packet word again and hears an intention become personal, without yet receiving the writer's full identity.

The evidence board offers observations, inferences and unanswered questions as separate spaces. The player places voice resemblance under inference. The safe-retreat instruction belongs under recorded fact. Nobody announces a death, a disappearance or a secret betrayal. The old story concerns an unfinished trial whose people had procedures and choices. Mei asks for the copy to be sent respectfully to Ferreira. The player keeps the original labels on both voices. What makes the scene intimate is not an instant reveal, but the discovery that somebody once cared about the same small yellow flower before these cadets knew it existed.

scenes.prose:
The Earth path is available, but the transmit queue does not make every question urgent. Rafi assembles a small evidence package: the intact reconstructed copy, its source photographs, the checksum and the transcript. Mei removes a line that guesses the gardener's name. The report becomes shorter and more honest.

The player checks which files were actually sent and which are merely saved locally. A receipt confirms delivery of the package. It is not a live answer from Ferreira and does not prove she agrees with the team's interpretation. Amara makes the distinction visible by placing the receipt in a separate column from future replies.

Kai wants to sit in front of the screen until somebody answers. Rafi suggests finishing the ordinary evening handover instead. The player verifies that the living plants have their care record and the tools have returned to their places. The mystery can wait without making the crew careless. A cup is placed at the mission table beside the pending reply indicator. Aurora has enough quiet for anticipation. Then the cup begins to tremble, and the ordinary object that made the room feel like home becomes the first observation of a new problem.

scenes.location: Interior brace zone beside mission table
scenes.prose:
The cup rattles again. Rafi looks down before he looks towards the screen. The shaking belongs to the station, not the recorder's speakers. A local structural alarm identifies the event as part of the fictional expedition scenario. The player moves each crew token to the marked interior brace zone and confirms four names.

No dexterity timer asks the learner to prove courage. The objective is to recognise the changing situation and use the prepared local response. Loose items are represented by clear prompts, while the game prevents a detour back to the garden controls during the active shaking. The plants remain in their serviced chambers; the crew does not run into another hazard to rescue a pot.

When the movement stops, Amara compares the atmosphere panel with its previous state. One indicator has turned red. Rafi holds the roll call until everyone answers and Kai points out a newly displaced service cover. Mei looks once at the pending Earth reply, then closes that panel. The older story remains unfinished, but the current problem takes priority. Chapter 2 ends with all four crew accounted for and the next action already understandable: trust the alarm enough to investigate, then test what it claims before touching a valve.

scenes.title: The Red Shape on the Screen
scenes.prose:
The oxygen-tank symbol is red. Amara reads it once, then again, while the player hears the familiar fans continue. The quake has stopped, but a warning still needs a reason. Reaching for the most dramatic valve would turn an interpretation into an action before the evidence is ready.

Rafi retrieves the independent mechanical gauge. The player checks its reference position, compares the main display with the local instrument and records the disagreement. The station remains in a controlled local response state. Nobody removes a helmet or enters an unverified space to create a thrilling shortcut. Kai offers a guess; Amara writes it under hypothesis rather than fault.

Mei checks the garden's local sealed atmosphere and reports that its chamber is separate from the room feed. That observation narrows what a garden-line isolation could affect. The player puts a simplified piping diagram beside the two readings and marks the locations each instrument actually measures. For the first time, Amara says she does not yet trust her interpretation. The admission does not make her less useful. It gives the team a question precise enough to test, and a safe reason to leave the valve untouched for one more check.

scenes.title: Three Taps, One Falling Line
scenes.prose:
Three labelled taps connect the simplified diagram to real service points. The player takes readings in a controlled sequence, recording the same observation interval at each. The main tank holds while the garden spur falls. A third point helps confirm which side of the branch contains the change. These are game profiles, not instructions for repairing real pressure equipment.

Kai traces the lines with his finger and initially puts the fault upstream of the wrong junction. The player tests that drawing against all three readings. It explains one observation but fails another. Amara does not simply replace his answer with her own. She asks which predicted reading would distinguish the two locations.

The comparison turns a red symbol into a narrow fault region. Mei asks whether isolating the branch will remove the plants' atmosphere. Rafi reads back the local-chamber check completed earlier. The crew can now reason from the same diagram rather than from four separate fears. The player saves the three readings with their positions and marks the proposed isolation boundary. The next action will be justified by what changes on each side, not by who sounded most certain.

scenes.title: Choose the Smallest Safe Boundary
scenes.prose:
The player places the proposed isolation on a paused copy of the atmosphere diagram. One preview closes the habitat trunk. Another isolates the garden spur while leaving the main habitat supplied. Both drawings stop flow somewhere, but only one preserves the required services while targeting the supported fault.

Amara asks the player to predict the gauge pattern before running either preview. The simulation then shows the changed lines and the services affected. A mistaken plan is informative because it remains a preview; the crew does not pay for an educational comparison with real harm. Rafi marks the approved sequence and the rollback condition beside it.

Ferreira's Earth channel is available for this authored contact window. She sends the relevant technical repair diagram immediately. It contains no personal confession and no missing procedure withheld behind a story puzzle. Kai checks the diagram against the physical labels rather than assuming an old drawing must still match the room. The team finishes with an agreed isolation, a check that will prove it worked and a way to stop if it does not. Mystery has no priority over a service line that needs making safe.

scenes.title: The Clamp and the Read-Back
scenes.storyTime: 2046-05-06 night through May 07 early hours UTC

Kai holds the approved sequence beside the physical labels. Amara reads each step back from the safe console while Rafi confirms that no one has crossed into the isolated work area. The player closes the garden spur, checks the mechanical pressure hold and seats the provided clamp through the authorised interface.

The repair has more than an installation animation. The player checks position, compares the gauge trend and reopens the line slowly under the scripted test profile. If the profile does not hold in the practice comparison, the interface returns to the diagnostic boundary rather than rewarding a completed hand movement. A clamp is useful because the verified system response changes.

Mei watches the plant-chamber record throughout. The chamber remained supported locally while the room branch was isolated, and its status is checked again before normal tending resumes. Kai wants to straighten a crooked label. Amara asks him to leave the evidence visible until the test is saved. For once, a slightly untidy room is a sign of careful work. The player restores the approved service configuration only after the hold check agrees with the independent gauge, and the crew can explain which part of the problem has actually been solved.

scenes.title: Five Checks Before a Quiet Room
scenes.location: Atmosphere console and restored garden spur
scenes.prose:
The repaired line produces an ordinary-looking graph. Amara refuses to call ordinary the same as unimportant. The player performs the five canonical checks, connecting each result to a service boundary or independent observation. The task is to show stability, not to keep clicking until a celebration appears.

Rafi asks another crew member to read the final sequence without Amara prompting. Kai finds a mismatch between a copied note and the current valve position. The player corrects the note, not the physical state that has already passed its test. This is a deliberate distinction between fixing documentation and undoing a sound repair. Mei records the garden's return to normal service.

The immediate repair is verified before the chapter moves into the following morning. Extended monitoring will continue into May 8, while nonhazardous camera investigation becomes possible on May 7. The handover grants camera-only annex inspection for May 7 and keeps suited entry pending the extended checks on May 8. When the warning clears, Amara leaves the independent gauge on its hook. She has learned a repeatable way to ask a good question, not a reason to distrust every screen forever.

scenes.title: A Door We Knew Was There
scenes.prose:
A displaced floor cover exposes the service hatch marked N.R. The annex was on the station's certified plan all along, isolated and nonessential. What the quake has revealed is an old access surface and its personal traces, not an entire unmapped room under a supposedly checked habitat.

The player matches the hatch to the supplied safety drawing, disconnects its utility feed and verifies the pressure boundary before opening a viewing port. A camera goes first. Physical entry is a separate later operation with suits and further clearance. The view shows tray silhouettes, a damaged growth chart and an old route marker under clear cover.

Ferreira provides technical context over the valid Earth path. An earlier trial ended before flowering, and the annex must be treated as an isolated service space. She does not yet confess her own role or identify the writer. Mei wants to move closer, but Rafi holds the camera steady until the required checks finish. His hands stay on the camera controls while the final boundary reading settles. Mei moves closer only when he turns the supported view towards her. The player saves the view and closes the port, knowing exactly what must happen before anyone may step through.

scenes.title: The Garden That Never Opened
scenes.location: Cold annex and warm-side support station
scenes.prose:
The suited entry begins only after the continuing checks are complete. Mei and Rafi inspect from the cold side while Kai and Amara support the controlled operation from the warm-side station. Their local radios stay available. The player sees the boundary crossing rather than appearing inside through an unexplained cut.

The trays contain frozen seedlings. None has flowered. Mei first sees the shape she expected to find, then corrects it when the growth chart and curled seedling leaves agree. A first bloom in their fictional lunar history remains a real achievement even though earlier people tried. The old trial is a beginning interrupted, not a secretly completed garden that erases the current story.

The player records evidence without pulling the plants apart. A service tag dates the trial to 2034; the route sheet was filed before evacuation. No clue demands a perilous recovery at the last moment of a retreat. Rafi reads back their return condition before the scene lingers on the unfinished labels. Mei leaves the tray as it is. Respecting what cannot be repaired is a different kind of care from saving Alo, and the player has to perform it with the same attention.

scenes.title: A Map Is a Plan to Verify
scenes.location: Annex chart archive and habitat evidence table
scenes.prose:
Under a sealed cover lies a route sheet towards a permanently shadowed survey site. A marked storage deposit appears beside an old authorised traversal, with its date before the final evacuation. The player connects the map to the trial records and sees why the vault could have been placed safely on an earlier survey rather than by an impossible last-minute journey.

Kai asks whether they should leave immediately. Rafi brings up current duties, route uncertainty and the need for a prepared return. A map is evidence that somebody planned a journey; it is not certification that the present rover can repeat it unchanged. The player records which details need a future slope, reserve and communications check.

Back in the habitat, care takes priority. Dated visits from May 8 to May 16 show the current pollinated plants developing pods while the annex record is archived. The chapter advances through purposeful observations, not a blank wait. Mei compares actual pod development with the life-cycle sequence assembled earlier. The two investigations now support each other: the old map gives a future objective, and the living experiment teaches when patience is required before starting it.

scenes.title: The Pod Is Not Ready Because We Are
scenes.prose:
Alo has changed while the crew repaired the room and read the annex. The flowers have given way to pods. Mei checks them against the maturity record instead of reaching for the harvest tray. Their experiment is succeeding, but success has made the plant less like the portrait everyone remembers.

The player compares maturity observations, checks the provided moisture profile and begins the canonical controlled dry-down. A preview contrasts opening the pods immediately with waiting for verified drying conditions. The premature path does not execute on the living plant; it shows why the planned sequence needs evidence. The five-day interval is named on the date card before the player accepts it.

Kai offers to change a lamp setting to make Alo look better. Amara distinguishes the end of a rapid plant's life cycle from a fault that can be repaired by more power. Mei does not need to understand every feeling before carrying out good care. She records the stage, approves the safe drying sequence and asks the others to remain nearby. The player completes the observation that allows the next step, learning that protecting a living process sometimes means allowing it to finish rather than trying to keep one image unchanged.

scenes.title: Forty-Two Sounds on a Tray
scenes.prose:
A dry petal rests against the chamber wall. The player verifies the final drying condition, then opens the mature pods over a contained tray. Small seed sounds replace the music for a moment. Alo has naturally finished her life; the scene does not revive her or present ordinary maturity as a preventable failure.

The player groups and counts the harvest, then cross-checks the total against the collected record. Forty-two seeds become two allocations: twelve for planting and thirty for the protected founder reserve. A test layout that double-counts one group fails the reconciliation before anything is sealed. Counting is a shared responsibility, not a trick about fast clicking.

Mei says she thought good care would mean longer. Amara answers that it allowed the plant to finish. Kai asks whether they should wait; Mei asks them to stay. The player sleeves the pressed petal and places its label beside the lineage record. The emotional outcome and the numerical ledger belong in the same scene. Alo is gone as one plant, but the work has produced a future that would not exist without her and Tara. The final total is read aloud before either seed container leaves the bench.

scenes.title: The Next Small Thing
scenes.location: Garden planting rack and reserve store
scenes.prose:
Twelve labelled positions wait on the next tray. Mei sets the first allocated seed into a cassette while Amara reads the parent line: Alo times Tara. The old flower's name does not erase the partner that helped make the harvest. Rafi holds the thirty-seed reserve container beside its seal record until the player confirms it has not been drawn from.

Planting twelve is an allocation already made, not a new reward generated by revisiting the bench. The player matches each planted position to the inventory and checks the separate protected reserve. A prediction view shows how removing another founder seed would change the ledger, so the crew can distinguish current planting from future descendants.

Kai asks what they will call the new plants. Mei lets everyone choose a dedication for the tray after the scientific labels are complete. A warm name can coexist with a precise lineage. The first new seed receives the same close framing as Alo's original planting, then the view widens to show all four cadets. The work feels less like replacing a lost mascot and more like taking responsibility together. The player finishes by putting the pressed petal somewhere it can be seen without being mistaken for a living original plant.

scenes.title: Five Months Are Made of Days
scenes.location: Aurora dated maintenance and lineage board
scenes.prose:
The calendar does not jump from one bright tray to another without an account. The player prepares a maintenance handover covering crop care, repeated compatible pollination, stored procedures, resupply planning and the safe operation of the habitat. Each dated chapter of the montage contains an observation or planning check that belongs to the intervening work.

The family tree shows several generations replacing annual plants. Twelve current descendants in October are not the twelve original seedlings kept unchanged for five months. The founder reserve remains its own protected record, while later harvests and care appear as ordinary generation records without invented fixed totals. Scheduled supplies and approved maintenance keep the crew supported; one mustard plant never becomes its food or oxygen system.

Mei places the pressed petal beside the first lineage photograph. Amara opens the saved stem-colour prediction and leaves it attached to a future October comparison. The old vault map moves from a mystery page to a prepared survey board, with current route and return checks still required. When the final date card settles on October 21, the garden is larger and the corridor familiar. The crew has not escaped the ordinary work between adventures. That work is what makes the next expedition possible.

scenes.title: What Actually Grew
scenes.location: Aurora descendant rack and prediction notebook
scenes.prose:
Before Rafi can open the rover checklist, Mei places the old stem prediction beside the current garden. The player inspects twelve current descendants, recording seven purple stems and five green in this authored observation. The game does not present this small fictional sample as a verified genetic ratio.

Amara asks the player to compare the actual observation with the prediction saved in May. A confident prediction can be wrong without making the investigation a failure. An uncertain prediction can gain information without pretending it was secretly correct all along. The original entry remains visible, with the new evidence added beside it rather than written over it.

Kai asks which seed was Alo. Mei points to the parent line, not a surviving original plant. The pressed petal and founder photograph are archived nearby; the present plants belong to continuing generations. The player checks the thirty-seed founder reserve separately from the twelve current descendants. Counting these plants does not spend or replenish those protected founder seeds. Rafi closes the comparison with one question: what observation should they make next? The answer becomes a new journal question, while the safe route expedition proceeds with the lesson already earned: a useful prediction leads back to evidence.

scenes.title: Two Seats Out, Two Voices Home
scenes.location: Rover bay and base handover screen
scenes.prose:
Rafi checks the rover twice, then admits it was three times. Kai starts to tease him and stops when Ferreira formally assigns field leadership. Caution has become a qualification. Two occupied rover seats appear beside the home-team screen: Rafi and Kai go; Mei and Amara remain at Aurora.

The player prepares the rover seal, scanner, closed carrier and independent consumables manifest. The base ledger accounts only for the two people staying home. The rover's dated round trip has its own support manifest, so the same occupants are not charged twice. The interface lets the player trace each person from the name list to the correct ledger.

Mei sends the map and current garden status. Amara holds the detailed slope card, while the field team will supply the headlight view. Neither perspective alone contains the whole route. Rafi asks for the handover in plain words before the hatch closes. Kai checks the spare light once, reads the labelled position and leaves it there. The habit recalls April without pretending his fear is cured. The team leaves a station with people in it, and takes a plan that has room for returning.

scenes.title: The Short Road Is Not the Safe Road
scenes.location: Shared route preview and rover navigation display
scenes.prose:
The old map becomes three current route cards. Route A is short but too steep for the rover. Route C is darker and also exceeds its slope limit while consuming the return reserve. Route B follows a longer ridge with an acceptable slope and a supported round trip. Kai sees the short line first; Amara's base card adds what its attractive distance does not show.

The player predicts reserve after both outbound and return travel, then compares that result with the slope constraint. In the canonical game profile, route B uses thirty units each way from a hundred, leaving forty against a required thirty. Its twelve-degree maximum remains below the fifteen-degree rover limit. These are scenario values, not a surveyed lunar road certification.

The route does not become valid because the player found a clever way to ignore one requirement. Both limits must hold. Rafi records the reason for rejecting each alternative, allowing the base team to understand the decision rather than merely receive it. Kai moves the short-route card aside himself. Beyond the rover window, the ridge bends out of sight. Their next job is making sure the radio plan can bend with it.

scenes.title: Put the Link Before the Corner
scenes.location: Surveyed ridge and three beacon positions
scenes.prose:
The first bend hides the station behind a ridge. Rafi stops before the blind corner, not after the base voice disappears. The player places a beacon on its surveyed mount, tests the link and confirms that it reaches the next segment. A neat-looking marker does not count unless its communication test passes.

The same reasoning develops across three short playable route segments. One site has a clear view but an unsuitable local mounting position; another has an approved mount but needs its relay alignment checked. The player combines the base slope card with the rover's close view to select the supported position at each authored checkpoint. Cruise between the segments is labelled rather than presented as empty driving time.

Kai watches a small link indicator settle beside each name. He calls the beacons little returning lights. Rafi accepts the description and keeps the engineering labels. Local radio remains the channel between the two field and two home cadets. No Earth voice substitutes for an untested ridge link. At the final corner, the player can trace an unbroken chain home on the map. The expedition has earned its view into the cold place by checking how its observations will get back.

scenes.title: A Bright Patch Is Not a Report
scenes.prose:
Headlights brighten a patch of ground, and Kai wants to call it ice. Amara asks for the dry reference first. The player records the scanner's reference signal and compares sample readings using the canonical threshold rule. A low reading remains a negative control even when the image looks interesting.

The game profile gives a dry reference of two and a threshold ten units above it. Two samples exceed that threshold; one does not. The player tags the supported positives and keeps the negative result instead of hiding it from the report. The instrument scale is an educational scenario profile, not a claim of newly measured lunar water from this fictional expedition.

Rafi repeats one reading from the same controlled contact position, and the comparison agrees. Mei watches the base evidence board gain a useful map of where the signal differs. No one promises a drink or an instant mining system. The next sample is collected because evidence supports ice-bearing material, not because a bright pixel deserves a treasure animation. The player saves the control, threshold and sample positions together, giving the eventual laboratory record enough context to be challenged and understood.

scenes.title: Something With Corners
scenes.location: Cold-trap sample point and vault approach
scenes.prose:
The sealed sample enters its holder. As Kai turns the light back towards the survey marker, a manufactured corner appears beyond it. The shape belongs to an insulated case, not to the rock. Mei sees the match to the recovered map on the base screen while Rafi checks their present position and return forecast.

The player records the sample context before moving to the case. Two discoveries do not become one mixed bag of evidence. The sample retains its position and calibrated result; the vault gets a separate photographic record, marker match and handling assessment. Kai brushes only the external identification window with the approved tool. The biological seal stays closed.

The old deposit date agrees with the earlier authorised route. Somebody intended the case to outlast a disrupted mission, but the game offers no certainty yet about who or what survived inside. Rafi tethers the closed carrier alongside the vault and asks the player to check reserve before beginning recovery. Curiosity has created a new task, not permission to forget the return plan. The final photograph shows both case and marker, making the discovery understandable even to someone who was never there.

scenes.exitCondition: Sample sealed, case provenance saved and recovery carrier secured.

scenes.title: The Lid Can Wait
scenes.prose:
Kai can see lettering beneath the lid and asks whether a quick look would save work later. Mei answers from the warm base that the lid can wait. The player checks the outer shell with the provided probe and compares the handling band with the carrier specification. The case's exterior temperature does not reveal the full history of its insulated inner specimens.

The paused recovery study contrasts opening the inner seal now with keeping it closed through insulated transport and sealed warming. Feedback shows why recovery must manage both temperature change and contamination. The game does not teach that every seed can survive any lunar soil temperature. It treats the fictional case as a protected experiment whose viability still needs assessment.

Rafi arranges the probe, sleeve and cradle in the approved sequence. Kai moves the light to make the actual labels readable instead of trying to see hidden text early. The player verifies the equipment before either astronaut lifts. A mystery that began with a drawer now depends on resisting the same impulse to open everything immediately. The crew can bring the question home intact, which is a better achievement than answering it badly in the cold.

learning.transfer: Transport a sample in a suitable labelled container before assessing it.

scenes.exitCondition: Handling band checked and sealed recovery sequence approved.

scenes.title: The Whole Box Comes Home
scenes.location: Vault cradle, rover cargo mount and local link
scenes.prose:
The player seats the insulated sleeve before beginning the lift. Rafi and Kai each take the indicated support point, with the carrier tethered and the rover cradle ready. The scene shows the object moving continuously from its deposit position to its secured cargo mount. Kai keeps the handle within the lit work area until the cradle carries its weight and Rafi confirms the restraint.

A latch indicates position with a word and symbol. A second check verifies that the mount is actually locked. The player compares those two results and records the sealed specimen carrier separately from the geological sample. Each object has its own handling needs, even though both will travel in the same vehicle.

Mei asks for the final exterior photograph before the team departs. It records what was removed and what was left undisturbed. Amara checks the revised cargo-and-return forecast, with the two rover occupants still on their own manifest. Kai looks at the closed lid once more, then clips the last tether. They have not been rewarded with a name. They have performed the part of the investigation that makes a trustworthy answer possible later. Rafi calls the base to confirm that the case is travelling home, not that the mystery has been solved.

scenes.title: Bring Back the Evidence and the People
scenes.location: Ridge return route and Aurora airlock
scenes.prose:
The return uses the same approved ridge, and the player checks the beacon chain from the other direction. A route that worked outbound still needs its return observations. The game selects short meaningful segments around link and reserve checks, with labelled cruise between them rather than empty kilometres of driving.

At each handover, the base team receives a status report containing occupants, cargo, pressure and remaining reserve. Kai notices how much less he has to remember when the report has the same structure every time. Rafi asks Amara to predict the final reserve from the current reading before the last segment resolves. The result is compared with the forecast, not silently overwritten to make the story work.

Aurora receives two returning cadets, a sealed sample and a sealed case on October 22. The forty-eight-hour rover consumables manifest covers this dated round trip. The player finishes the airlock sequence and transfers the vault to the dry quarantine glovebox while the inner seal remains shut. Only now do all four cadets share the same physical room again. Mei rests her hand near the case without touching its lid. Home has made the next question safe to ask.

scenes.title: Twelve Wells, Twelve Questions
scenes.prose:
The case warms while sealed, under a controlled profile in the dry glovebox. The player checks that the stabilisation criterion is met before breaking the biological seal inside that protected workspace. Warming is not represented as proof that every seed is viable. It is the next careful step towards assessing what was preserved.

Twelve distinct specimen wells appear beneath the lid, including cotton. The player matches each label with the case manifest and creates a separate condition entry. An illustrated collection page can record knowledge about a specimen, but it does not add another physical seed. The founder reserve and current garden remain on different pages with different counts.

Kai recognises cotton from the first chapter's real-history reference. Mei asks everyone to keep the whole collection safe before choosing a future planting. None is consumed in this scene. The full physical vault inventory remains twelve until cotton is planted later in December, after which eleven other specimens remain stored. The player scans the lid only after the handling work is complete. The reward arrives as a line of handwriting, supported by a chain of decisions that has kept both the object and its meaning intact.

scenes.title: Ask Commander Ferreira
scenes.location: Glovebox scan station and Earth console
scenes.prose:
The handwriting asks the finder to speak to Commander Ferreira about Expedition Zero. It supplies a connection, not the complete story. Mei reads the line once, then sends a clear image and the reconciled manifest through the available Earth path. Nobody supplies a name from initials alone.

The player compares what the new evidence changes. The case was intentionally preserved; the trial had a human history; Ferreira is the appropriate person to ask. It does not establish that the writer died, that the commander abandoned anyone or that the seed specimens will all grow. Those conclusions remain outside the acquired evidence.

Ferreira's channel is quiet for a moment. Rao confirms the technical receipt and approved safety instructions, keeping personal hesitation separate from operational support. Mei chooses how to phrase an invitation to explain, without turning disclosure into a coercive dialogue puzzle. Kai begins a joke and lets it go. The crew can feel that a familiar adult has a difficult connection to their discovery. That feeling gives the scene weight without replacing the Chapter 5 reveal. The player saves the exact inscription and the unanswered question together, allowing the next chapter to answer what this one has honestly earned.

scenes.title: A Fifth Mug Has a Journey
scenes.prose:
Kai puts a fifth mug beside the four familiar ones. Amara adds it to the inventory before anyone can describe the gesture as reckless generosity. The spare place belongs to a scheduled traveller. Kai reads the flight notice before putting her name on the locker.

The player reads the relief assignment: Ferreira departs Earth on December 8 and arrives on December 12 with the planned support flight. Rao remains at the Earth console. Hardware, quarantine supplies and routine habitat needs are checked against the cargo manifest, while the current garden and protected specimens retain their care plan. This is resupply supporting an operating base, not an unexplained ability to survive indefinitely on a mustard flower.

Ferreira promises to bring the personal story. She does not ask the crew to postpone a safety check until then. The player prepares her locker, verifies the fifth-occupant handover for arrival and confirms the dated October-to-December maintenance transition. Photos and care entries show the intervening work. At the final date card the mug is still waiting, and the player can name the route that brought its owner. A room once made for four is ready to listen to a fifth person who will have to speak as herself.
